Let B be an “extraction attacker” that takes the outcome y and aims to compute a short program A that serves as an extraction evidence for S w.r.t. a relation R and a programming language L. We show that if M is Narcissus-resilient (w.r.t. an appropriate reconstruction relation), then it prevents B from succeeding in its attack. Formally, ▶ Definition 19. Fix a parameter q ≤ 1 controlling the desired quality of extraction (as in Definition 13). We define the relation Rext that takes a dataset S and a pair (y, A) where y is an outcome of M and A is a program, and returns 1 if and only if the following two conditions hold: 1. R(S, A(y)) = 1, and |A| 2. KL ({z : R(S,z)=1}) ≤ 1 − q.
